findings.summary: CODEX-06-A meets every current acceptance criterion. It adds a finite fixture-1/fixture-engine-1 engine that strictly checks the full adventure 1.1.0 and play_action 1.1.0 shapes, and every rejection leaves state unchanged. The React player gets its outcomes only from the engine and is reached only through the existing three-flag preview predicate. The outcome stays hidden until a committed prediction and configuration reach Test. Only the one designated variable (balanced/offset) can change. Retained tries show the guess, position and result immutably, unsupported specs and actions fail safely, and two tries need only button taps. Controller evidence on this tree is real and passing: 19 node tests, the Vite build, a contract-level engine probe, a jsdom DOM probe that transpiles the actual TSX and clicks real handlers, 36 main.tsx routing cases, and a seeded production secret scan. The remaining notes are minor quality items. Browser, phone and layout QA is honestly reported as not observed.

findings.title: No repo-maintained component test; DOM coverage lives only in controller probe
findings.problem: The card asks app tests to cover 'real component interaction as appropriate'. The repository tests exercise only the engine. React/jsdom interaction (Test gating, retained fields, invalid-prop alert) is verified only by the controller's player_dom_probe.mjs, so a future `npm test` would not catch UI regressions such as Test enabling early or current-result rendering before Test. Acceptable under 'as appropriate' because the controller probe is real and passed, but this should be tracked.
findings.fix_check: A later card or follow-up adds a maintained jsdom component test under tests/ (or explicitly records that the controller probe is the maintained UI regression gate).

findings.title: Compare control only offers the latest two tries
findings.problem: The engine accepts any two distinct retained trial IDs, but the UI sends only `trials.slice(-2)`. Every try stays visible, so the criterion holds. However, with three or more tries a child or parent cannot ask to compare, for example, try 1 with try 3. That limits the comparison step of PD-007/F08.
findings.fix_check: Either let users choose two retained tries to compare, or record that latest-two comparison is an intentional v1 simplification for CODEX-06-B/C to revisit.

findings.title: Rejection message implies inputs were lost
findings.problem: On any dispatch rejection the UI says 'Choose your guess and position again.' Rejections leave state unchanged, so the committed inputs are still selected (aria-pressed stays true). The message can mislead a parent or child. It is a wording problem only, not a safety one.
findings.fix_check: The message wording matches the unchanged state (for example, 'That didn't work. Your choices are still selected; try again.').

findings.title: Engine reads action.kind before descriptor validation
findings.problem: `switch (action.kind)` runs before `exact()` confirms that `kind` is an own data property, so a caller-supplied getter would run once before rejection. No state changes and the UI never sends such input, but strict 'no hidden effects' validation would check the shape first.
findings.fix_check: Check the action's own keys or data descriptors (or read the `kind` descriptor value) before branching on kind.

findings.title: Report cites a different task blob than the canonical card header
findings.problem: REPORT.md pins task blob 35cf6bfb… under APPROVAL-003, but the card header supplied for this review names source blob 4ef4aa86… (commit 70a195e…). These may be the normalized canonical copy versus the source, but the report does not say which, which weakens the exact-revision provenance the card requires.
findings.fix_check: REPORT.md states which artifact each blob identifies (canonical approved copy vs. source) and they reconcile with approved/APPROVALS.md.
